title: Cubic Taylor polynomial under matched moments
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $\mathbb E X=0$, $\mathbb E X^2=1$, $\mathbb E X^3=0$, and $\mathbb E X^4\le 9$, and suppose $X$ is measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment. For every function $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and all $a,b\in\mathbb R$, the expectation of $\sum_{j=0}^{3}\frac{\psi^{(j)}(a)}{j!}(bX)^j$ is $\psi(a)+\frac{\psi^{(2)}(a)}{2}b^2$, where the derivatives are iterated derivatives.
hypotheses_covered: $X$ is measurable up to a null set and has finite fourth absolute moment
replaced: Let $X$ be a real input on a probability space, measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment, first three moments $0,1,0$, and fourth moment at most $9$. For any real function $\psi$ and real $a,b$, $\mathbb E[\sum_{j=0}^3\psi^{(j)}(a)(bX)^j/j!]=\psi(a)+\tfrac12\psi^{(2)}(a)b^2$. Here iterated differentiation assigns zero at a point where the derivative does not exist, so the identity requires no smoothness of $\psi$.
